title: 1 Corinthians Chapter 13 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 1 Corinthians chapter 13 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 1 Corinthians Chapter 13 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 1 Corinthians Chapter 13.

questions.question: In 1 Corinthians 13, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Speaking with the tongues of men and of angels
Bestowing all goods to feed the poor
questions.correctAnswer: Speaking with the tongues of men and of angels
questions.explanation: This appears first as stated in 1 Corinthians 13:1.

questions.question: What happens if one speaks with the tongues of men and of angels but has not charity?
options: They are become as sounding brass
questions.correctAnswer: They are become as sounding brass
questions.explanation: This is stated in 1 Corinthians 13:1.

questions.question: What is mentioned as a gift one might have in 1 Corinthians 13:2?
questions.explanation: The gift of prophecy is mentioned in 1 Corinthians 13:2.

questions.question: According to 1 Corinthians 13:2, what can one have that allows them to remove mountains?
questions.explanation: Having all faith that could remove mountains is mentioned in 1 Corinthians 13:2.

questions.question: What does one gain by bestowing all goods to feed the poor without charity?
questions.explanation: It states that it profiteth nothing in 1 Corinthians 13:3.

questions.question: What characteristic of charity is mentioned first in 1 Corinthians 13:4?
questions.explanation: Charity suffereth long is the first characteristic listed in 1 Corinthians 13:4.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a behavior of charity according to 1 Corinthians 13:5?
questions.explanation: Charity is described as not easily provoked in 1 Corinthians 13:5.

questions.question: What does charity NOT do according to 1 Corinthians 13:4?
questions.explanation: Charity envieth not is specifically mentioned in 1 Corinthians 13:4.

questions.question: What is the consequence of giving one's body to be burned without charity according to 1 Corinthians 13:3?
questions.explanation: It clearly states in 1 Corinthians 13:3 that it profiteth me nothing.

questions.question: According to 1 Corinthians 13:5, charity thinketh what?
questions.explanation: Charity thinketh no evil is stated in 1 Corinthians 13:5.

questions.question: Charity is described as what in 1 Corinthians 13:4?
questions.explanation: Charity is described as kind in 1 Corinthians 13:4.

questions.question: True or False: Charity vaunteth itself according to 1 Corinthians 13:4.
questions.explanation: Charity vaunteth not itself is stated in 1 Corinthians 13:4.

questions.question: True or False: Charity is easily provoked according to 1 Corinthians 13:5.
questions.explanation: Charity is not easily provoked as per 1 Corinthians 13:5.

questions.question: True or False: Charity is described as suffering short according to 1 Corinthians 13:4.
questions.explanation: Charity suffereth long is the correct phrase in 1 Corinthians 13:4.

questions.question: True or False: The gift of prophecy is mentioned in 1 Corinthians 13:2.
questions.explanation: The gift of prophecy is indeed mentioned in 1 Corinthians 13:2.

medium.title: 1 Corinthians Chapter 13 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 1 Corinthians Chapter 13 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What does love (charity) not rejoice in according to 1 Corinthians 13:6?
questions.explanation: Charity does not rejoice in iniquity, but rejoices in the truth, as stated in 1 Corinthians 13:6.

questions.question: What does 1 Corinthians 13:7 promise will happen if someone bears all things?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 13:7 states that charity bears all things and endures all things, indicating a promise of endurance.

questions.question: According to 1 Corinthians 13:8, what will never fail?
questions.explanation: Charity never faileth, as stated in 1 Corinthians 13:8, contrasting it with prophecies, tongues, and knowledge which will cease.

questions.question: What is true about our knowledge and prophecy according to 1 Corinthians 13:9?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 13:9 reveals that we know and prophesy in part, indicating our limited understanding.

questions.question: What will happen to that which is in part according to 1 Corinthians 13:10?
questions.explanation: When that which is perfect comes, that which is in part will be done away, as stated in 1 Corinthians 13:10.

questions.question: What characterizes love according to 1 Corinthians 13:4?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 13:4 describes charity as kind, emphasizing its nature as loving and patient.

questions.question: What does 1 Corinthians 13:2 say about having faith without charity?
questions.explanation: According to 1 Corinthians 13:2, having faith without charity means one is nothing, highlighting the importance of love.

questions.question: What does 1 Corinthians 13:5 say love does not think?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 13:5 states that charity thinketh no evil, illustrating the purity of true love.

questions.question: According to 1 Corinthians 13:3, what is the profit of giving all goods to feed the poor without charity?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 13:3 indicates that giving without charity profits nothing, stressing the value of love in actions.

questions.question: What does 1 Corinthians 13:1 say about speaking without charity?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 13:1 explains that speaking without charity results in being like sounding brass or tinkling cymbal, signifying emptiness.

questions.question: What aspect of charity is highlighted in 1 Corinthians 13:4 regarding pride?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 13:4 emphasizes that charity is not puffed up, indicating its humble nature.

questions.question: What does 1 Corinthians 13:6 indicate charity rejoices in?
questions.explanation: Charity rejoices in the truth, as stated in 1 Corinthians 13:6, contrasting with iniquity.

questions.question: Is it true that charity never fails according to 1 Corinthians 13:8?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 13:8 states that charity never faileth, affirming its eternal nature.

questions.question: Is it true that prophecies will last forever according to 1 Corinthians 13:8?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 13:8 indicates that prophecies shall fail, meaning they will not last forever.

questions.question: Is it true that we know everything fully according to 1 Corinthians 13:9?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 13:9 explains that we know in part, indicating our incomplete understanding.

hard.title: 1 Corinthians Chapter 13 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 1 Corinthians Chapter 13.

questions.question: According to 1 Corinthians 13:11, what does the apostle Paul say he did when he became a man?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 13:11 states, 'but when I became a man, I put away childish things,' indicating a transition from childish behaviors and thoughts to mature understanding.

questions.question: In 1 Corinthians 13:12, what metaphor is used to describe our current knowledge?
questions.explanation: The verse 1 Corinthians 13:12 uses the metaphor 'For now we see through a glass, darkly' to describe limited or partial knowledge in the present.

questions.question: What are the three virtues that 'abide' according to 1 Corinthians 13:13?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 13:13 states, 'And now abideth faith, hope, charity, these three;' identifying these as the enduring virtues.

questions.question: Which virtue is described as the greatest in 1 Corinthians 13:13?
questions.explanation: The verse 1 Corinthians 13:13 concludes with 'but the greatest of these is charity,' emphasizing its supreme importance.

questions.question: How does 1 Corinthians 13:12 describe the future state of knowledge?
options: Then face to face; then shall I know even as also I am known
Then we will see through a glass, clearly
Then shadows will be cast aside
Then mysteries will be revealed in part
questions.correctAnswer: Then face to face; then shall I know even as also I am known
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 13:12 contrasts current partial knowledge with future complete understanding 'then face to face: now I know in part; but then shall I know even as also I am known.'

questions.question: What childlike behaviors does Paul mention in 1 Corinthians 13:11 that he put away as he matured?
options: Spake as a child, understood as a child, thought as a child
Ran as a child, played as a child, laughed as a child
Feared as a child, doubted as a child, cried as a child
Prayed as a child, hoped as a child, dreamed as a child
questions.correctAnswer: Spake as a child, understood as a child, thought as a child
questions.explanation: The verse 1 Corinthians 13:11 explicitly states, 'I spake as a child, I understood as a child, I thought as a child: but when I became a man, I put away childish things.'

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'agape' (ἀγάπη) in 1 Corinthians 13:13 primarily mean?
questions.explanation: The Greek word 'agape' used in 1 Corinthians 13:13 denotes selfless, unconditional love which is central to Pauline theology and the theme of the chapter.

questions.question: Which literary device is predominantly used in 1 Corinthians 13:4-7 to describe charity?
questions.explanation: Verses 4-7 use anaphora, the repetition of 'charity' (love) at the beginning of several clauses, emphasizing its attributes and creating a rhythmic emphasis.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage echoes the theme of love's enduring nature as found in 1 Corinthians 13:8?
questions.explanation: Psalm 136:1 repeats 'His mercy endureth forever,' paralleling the enduring nature of love (charity) described in 1 Corinthians 13:8.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage fulfills the theme of seeing 'face to face' as described in 1 Corinthians 13:12?
questions.explanation: Revelation 22:4 says, 'They shall see his face,' fulfilling the theme of direct, face-to-face knowledge mentioned in 1 Corinthians 13:12.

questions.question: What immediately precedes 1 Corinthians 13:11 in the text?
options: But when that which is perfect is come, then that which is in part shall be done away.
For we know in part, and we prophesy in part.
And now abideth faith, hope, charity.
questions.correctAnswer: But when that which is perfect is come, then that which is in part shall be done away.
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 13:10 directly precedes verse 11, stating that the partial will be done away when the perfect comes, setting the stage for the metaphor about maturity in verse 11.

questions.question: How does Paul use typology in 1 Corinthians 13:11 to contrast spiritual maturity?
options: By likening spiritual growth to the transition from childhood to adulthood
By comparing charity to the sacrifices of the Old Testament
By paralleling tongues with angelic speech
By allegorizing faith as a shield
questions.correctAnswer: By likening spiritual growth to the transition from childhood to adulthood
questions.explanation: In 1 Corinthians 13:11, Paul uses the typology of childhood versus adulthood to symbolize the transition from partial to full spiritual understanding.

questions.question: What parallelism is evident in 1 Corinthians 13:7 regarding the qualities of charity?
options: Antithetic parallelism contrasting love and hate
Chiastic parallelism framing belief and hope
questions.explanation: Verse 7 lists qualities in sequence: 'Beareth all things, believeth all things, hopeth all things, endureth all things,' demonstrating sequential parallelism emphasizing the endurance of charity.

questions.question: True or False: According to 1 Corinthians 13:8, prophecies, tongues, and knowledge will eventually cease or vanish away, but charity will never fail.
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 13:8 clearly states that 'Charity never faileth: but whether there be prophecies, they shall fail; whether there be tongues, they shall cease; whether there be knowledge, it shall vanish away.'

questions.question: True or False: 1 Corinthians 13:12 states that we currently know fully and clearly as if face to face.
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 13:12 explains that 'For now we see through a glass, darkly; now I know in part; but then shall I know even as also I am known,' indicating current partial knowledge, not full and clear.

theological.title: 1 Corinthians Chapter 13 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 1 Corinthians Chapter 13 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does 1 Corinthians 13:1 teach about the necessity of charity for true spiritual communication?
options: Without charity, even angelic tongues are meaningless noise
Charity is only one spiritual gift among many
Charity is a minor virtue in spiritual life
questions.correctAnswer: Without charity, even angelic tongues are meaningless noise
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 13:1 emphasizes that speaking with the tongues of men and angels without charity results in being 'as sounding brass, or a tinkling cymbal,' indicating the essential nature of charity for meaningful spiritual communication.

questions.question: What doctrine does 1 Corinthians 13:2 teach about the relationship between faith and charity in the life of a believer?
options: Even faith capable of moving mountains profits nothing without charity
Faith alone is sufficient for spiritual maturity
Prophecy and knowledge outweigh charity in importance
questions.correctAnswer: Even faith capable of moving mountains profits nothing without charity
questions.explanation: According to 1 Corinthians 13:2, possessing all faith to remove mountains is of no profit if charity is absent, highlighting charity's primacy over even miraculous faith.

questions.question: What doctrine about sacrificial giving and charity does 1 Corinthians 13:3 teach?
options: Sacrifice guarantees divine approval regardless of motive
Charity and sacrifice are unrelated concepts
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 13:3 states that even giving all one’s goods or being burned alive profits nothing if charity is absent, teaching that the motive of charity is essential for true spiritual value in sacrifice.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 1 Corinthians 13:4 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 13:4 describes charity as suffering long and being kind, which corresponds directly to the divine attribute of longsuffering—God’s patient endurance with humanity.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 1 Corinthians 13:7 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 13:7 highlights that charity 'beareth all things, believeth all things, hopeth all things, endureth all things,' reflecting God's faithful and steadfast commitment to His people.

questions.question: How does 1 Corinthians 13:8–10 connect to the broader biblical theme of the partial and the perfect in redemptive history?
options: It portrays spiritual gifts as temporary until the coming of perfection
It denies the future perfection of knowledge
It teaches that prophecy is more important than charity
It claims knowledge is permanent and unchanging
questions.correctAnswer: It portrays spiritual gifts as temporary until the coming of perfection
questions.explanation: Verses 8–10 explain that prophecies, tongues, and knowledge will fail or vanish when 'that which is perfect is come,' connecting to biblical teaching on the partial nature of current revelation contrasted with ultimate perfection.

questions.question: How does 1 Corinthians 13:12 anticipate the eschatological vision of seeing God face to face in Scripture?
options: By contrasting present partial knowledge with future full knowledge
By denying any future improvement in understanding
By teaching that present knowledge is complete
By emphasizing the impossibility of knowing God fully
questions.correctAnswer: By contrasting present partial knowledge with future full knowledge
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 13:12 uses the metaphor of seeing 'through a glass, darkly' now but 'face to face' then, anticipating the eschatological hope of full revelation and knowledge of God.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 1 Corinthians 13:4 and 1 Corinthians 13:5 teach about the nature of charity?
options: Charity is patient, kind, and does not behave itself unseemly or seek its own
Charity is primarily about personal gain
Charity is limited to feelings of envy and pride
Charity encourages provocation and thinking evil
questions.correctAnswer: Charity is patient, kind, and does not behave itself unseemly or seek its own
questions.explanation: Verses 4 and 5 together describe charity as suffering long, being kind, not envying, not vaunting, not puffed up, not behaving unseemly, not seeking its own, and not easily provoked, defining its selfless nature.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 1 Corinthians 13:6 and 1 Corinthians 13:7 teach about charity’s ethical orientation?
options: Charity rejoices in truth and bears, believes, hopes, and endures all things
Charity rejoices in iniquity and condemns hope
Charity is indifferent to moral truth
questions.correctAnswer: Charity rejoices in truth and bears, believes, hopes, and endures all things
questions.explanation: Verses 6 and 7 affirm that charity does not rejoice in iniquity but in truth and that it bears, believes, hopes, and endures all things, showing an ethical orientation grounded in truth and perseverance.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 1 Corinthians 13:9 and 1 Corinthians 13:11 teach about the spiritual maturity of believers?
options: We know and prophesy in part, and must put away childish things as we mature
Spiritual maturity depends on perfect knowledge from the start
Prophecy and knowledge never develop over time
Childish understanding is preferable to mature faith
questions.correctAnswer: We know and prophesy in part, and must put away childish things as we mature
questions.explanation: Verse 9 acknowledges partial knowledge and prophecy, while verse 11 uses the metaphor of putting away childish things when becoming a man, teaching progressive spiritual maturity.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that 1 Corinthians 13:8-10 teaches that prophecy and knowledge are worthless. What does 1 Corinthians 13:8-10 actually teach?
options: Prophecies and knowledge are temporary and partial until the perfect comes
Prophecy and knowledge are completely useless at all times
Charity is less important than prophecy and knowledge
The perfect has already come, making prophecy obsolete
questions.correctAnswer: Prophecies and knowledge are temporary and partial until the perfect comes
questions.explanation: Verses 8-10 clarify that while prophecy and knowledge are important, they are partial and will cease when perfection arrives, not that they are worthless in themselves.

questions.question: What doctrine does 1 Corinthians 13:13 teach about the enduring qualities of faith, hope, and charity?
options: Faith, hope, and charity abide, with charity being the greatest
Only faith abides eternally, charity is temporary
Hope is greater than charity and faith
Charity is less important than faith and hope
questions.correctAnswer: Faith, hope, and charity abide, with charity being the greatest
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 13:13 concludes that faith, hope, and charity remain permanently, but charity is the greatest, emphasizing its supreme value.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is most clearly demonstrated by the description of charity in 1 Corinthians 13:6?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 13:6 states charity 'rejoiceth not in iniquity, but rejoiceth in the truth,' reflecting God's holiness and hatred of sin.

questions.question: How does 1 Corinthians 13:12 relate to the biblical doctrine of epistemology in theology?
options: It teaches that human knowledge of God is partial now but will be complete in the eschaton
It denies any possibility of knowing God
It claims current knowledge is perfect and unchanging
It suggests that God is unknowable forever
questions.correctAnswer: It teaches that human knowledge of God is partial now but will be complete in the eschaton
questions.explanation: Verse 12 explicitly contrasts our present partial, obscure knowledge with future clear, full knowledge 'as I am known,' teaching a progressive epistemology culminating in eschatological revelation.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 1 Corinthians 13:2 and 1 Corinthians 13:3 teach about the insufficiency of works without charity?
options: Prophecy, faith, and sacrificial giving profit nothing without charity
Works alone guarantee justification before God
Charity is unrelated to faith and works
questions.correctAnswer: Prophecy, faith, and sacrificial giving profit nothing without charity
questions.explanation: Verses 2 and 3 affirm that even possessing prophecy, faith to move mountains, or giving all goods and body to be burned profits nothing if charity is absent, teaching the insufficiency of works apart from love.
